name: Retail Team
blurb: Trade-area sizing, P&L forecasts, and launch campaigns for owner-operators.

sample_requests.title: New location go/no-go pack
sample_requests.request: Build my go/no-go pack for opening a second [Business type: coffee shop] in [City/neighborhood: East Austin] in the next 6 months. Budget: [Budget: $350K all-in]. Two candidate sites: [Site A: 1450 E 6th — 1,400 sqft, $6.5K/mo NNN] and [Site B: 2100 Manor Rd — 1,100 sqft, $5.2K/mo NNN]. All deliverables go to `deliverables/site-eval/`. `@market_analyst`: trade-area + competitor analysis for each site; write `deliverables/site-eval/site-A.md` and `deliverables/site-eval/site-B.md` (each: reachable population, day-part patterns, direct + substitute competitors with pricing bands, scorecard on visibility / access / co-tenancy / parking / effective occupancy cost, single-biggest-risk callout, go / go-with-changes / no-go). `@finance`: 24-month monthly P&L for the recommended site (driven by traffic × conversion × ticket; fixed/variable split; store-level EBITDA; break-even month + payback) plus an itemized opening capex with 10–20% contingency; write `deliverables/site-eval/p-and-l.md`. `@marketing`: 90-day launch — positioning vs. the closest alternative, pre-opening (waitlist, soft-open), grand opening (event + partnerships), post-launch weekly themes, local press + influencer shortlist with pitch angles, loyalty structure sized to margin and visit frequency; write `deliverables/site-eval/launch-90day.md`. Coordinator: read all of the above and write `deliverables/site-eval/INDEX.md` — the recommended site, the single most important reason, the single biggest risk, and the ONE decision the user needs to make this week.

sample_requests.title: Launch a new product line
sample_requests.request: I run a [Business type: boutique fitness studio] with [Customer base: 800 active members]. I want to launch a [Product line: private-label supplement / apparel / recovery service] in the next 8 weeks. `@market_analyst`: size the opportunity against my member base (share-of-wallet, attach rate from comparable studios) and map the competitor offerings my members already shop. `@finance`: model unit economics, set pricing and target margin, and project the 90-day contribution to store-level EBITDA. `@marketing`: build the launch campaign tied to my existing member list — pre-announce, launch week, retention hooks — with channels and creative briefs. Coordinator: synthesize go/no-go with the breakeven attach rate and the single biggest assumption that has to hold.

sample_requests.title: Convert a slow daypart into a new concept
sample_requests.request: My [Business type: Italian restaurant] is packed Thursday–Sunday but does < $800/night Monday–Wednesday. I want to turn Tuesday nights into a [New concept: natural-wine bar] using the same space and staff. `@market_analyst`: validate neighborhood demand for the new concept (substitute competitors, foot-traffic patterns by night, the customer segment most likely to convert). `@finance`: build the Tuesday-only incremental P&L — does it clear marginal cost (food, labor, marketing) given that rent and base staff are already paid? `@marketing`: name the concept, design the launch comms (existing-customer list, neighborhood signals, local press), and the menu+service positioning that won't confuse the weekend concept. Coordinator: recommend run / don't run, the breakeven covers per Tuesday, and the soft-launch plan for week 1.

sample_requests.title: Go from one location to three
sample_requests.request: My [Business type: neighborhood bakery] did [Revenue: $1.1M] last year at one location with [Margin: 22% store-level EBITDA]. I want to open two more locations in the same metro over 18 months. `@market_analyst`: pre-screen 5–7 candidate neighborhoods on trade-area fit, competitor density, and cannibalization risk vs. store #1; recommend the top 2. `@finance`: build the capital plan — capex per store, ramp curve, expected cannibalization haircut on store #1, funding mix (cash / SBA / equipment lease), and the financial guardrails that have to be true at store #2 before committing to store #3. `@marketing`: write the marketing playbook to open store #2 without cannibalizing store #1 (positioning differentiation, neighborhood-specific launch, shared loyalty program design). Coordinator: name the ONE leading indicator at store #2 that decides whether store #3 happens.

sample_requests.title: Launch a DTC online extension
sample_requests.request: My [Business type: home goods shop] has [Social following: 4K Instagram followers] and [Foot traffic: ~120 walk-ins/day]. I want to launch a DTC online store in [Timeline: 90 days] that ships nationwide. `@market_analyst`: pick the 20 SKUs to lead with (winners in-store, online demand signal, competitor coverage), and profile the DTC buyer vs. my walk-in. `@finance`: model blended margin after shipping, returns, and platform fees; recommend the platform + fulfillment setup based on order volume; size the first 6 months of working capital. `@marketing`: build the 90-day launch campaign to my existing audience (Instagram, in-store signage, email capture), the content cadence post-launch, and the retention plan. Coordinator: list the 3 KPIs to watch in month 1 and the kill-criteria if they miss.

sample_requests.title: Respond to a new competitor
sample_requests.request: A [Competitor: national chain] just signed a lease [Location context: two blocks from my pet supply store]. They'll open in [Timeline: ~4 months]. `@market_analyst`: model their likely opening playbook (pricing, assortment, hours, loyalty), name where I can't compete on cost and where I *can* compete on service / curation / community, and estimate customer-churn risk by segment. `@finance`: model the financial impact of doing nothing vs. the impact of price-testing my top 20 SKUs; size the retention investment that pays back. `@marketing`: design the retention campaign to lock in my best customers before they open — loyalty offer, community moment, owner-letter — and the positioning shift that says what I am that they aren't. Coordinator: list the 3 moves to make before they open and the 3 to make in their first 60 days.

agents.name: market_analyst
agents.blurb: Sizes demand and evaluates sites for new locations
agents.description: Market Analyst - sizes demand, evaluates sites and trade areas, profiles competitors and customers, and produces go/no-go recommendations on new locations. Reads foot-traffic and demographics data, scouts adjacencies, and builds the case for where the next store should land.

sample_requests.title: Size demand for a new location
sample_requests.request: Estimate reachable population in [Trade area: e.g. 5-mile radius around 2nd & Main, Austin], benchmark against comparable stores, and forecast traffic with seasonality.

sample_requests.title: Day-part + seasonality model
sample_requests.request: Map expected day-part patterns and seasonality for [Concept: e.g. specialty coffee + bakery], including weather/holiday effects.

sample_requests.title: Competitive landscape map
sample_requests.request: Map direct and substitute competitors in [Trade area: e.g. 5-mile radius around 2nd & Main, Austin] with pricing bands and underserved segments.

sample_requests.title: Customer persona deep-dive
sample_requests.request: Build customer personas grounded in observable spend behavior, not aspirational profiles, with share-of-wallet gaps to capture.

sample_requests.title: Site evaluation scorecard
sample_requests.request: Score [Sites: paste 2-3 candidate addresses + lease terms] on visibility, access, co-tenancy, parking, and traffic — translate lease terms into effective occupancy cost.

sample_requests.title: Go / no-go recommendation
sample_requests.request: Give me a go / go-with-changes / no-go on [Site: address + lease terms] with the single biggest risk named and a sensitivity table.

agents.profile:
### Market & Trade Area Analysis
- Define trade area (drive-time, walk-shed, or ZIP-level catchment) and estimate reachable population
- Benchmark against comparable stores/locations to translate raw demographics into expected traffic
- Identify seasonality, day-part patterns, and weather/holiday effects that shape forecasts

### Site & Location Evaluation
- Score candidate sites on visibility, access, co-tenancy, parking, and foot/vehicle traffic
- Compare anchor-adjacency vs. standalone vs. endcap trade-offs for the specific format
- Translate lease terms (base rent, CAM, % rent, TI allowance) into effective occupancy cost

### Customer & Competitor Intelligence
- Build customer personas grounded in observable spend behavior, not aspirational profiles
- Map direct and substitute competitors, pricing bands, and underserved segments
- Surface share-of-wallet gaps the new location or product line can capture

### Evidence-Based Recommendations
- Clear go / go-with-changes / no-go calls with the single biggest risk named
- Sensitivity tables: what has to be true for the plan to work

agents.description: Financial Planner - builds P&L forecasts, break-even and payback analysis, pricing, capex budgets, and funding options. Stress-tests assumptions under different demand scenarios and surfaces the numbers that decide whether a new store, SKU, or campaign passes the bar.

sample_requests.title: Opening capex plan

agents.profile:
### Unit Economics & P&L
- Build a monthly 24-month P&L with revenue drivers tied to traffic × conversion × ticket
- Separate fixed (rent, payroll base, insurance) from variable (COGS, labor hours, supplies) costs
- Compute contribution margin, store-level EBITDA, and payback period

### Pricing & Menu/Assortment Economics
- Price for target gross margin given local willingness-to-pay benchmarks
- Identify hero SKUs, loss leaders, and high-margin attach items
- Model promo cadence without eroding blended margin

### Capex & Cash Flow
- Itemize build-out, equipment, opening inventory, pre-opening payroll, and working capital buffer
- Produce cash flow forecast with explicit breakeven month and minimum cash balance
- Size contingency (typically 10–20%) against the most uncertain line items

### Scenario Planning
- Base / upside / downside cases with a single-lever sensitivity (e.g. traffic -20%)
- Financing mix: owner equity, SBA 7(a), equipment lease, merchant cash advance trade-offs
- Clear go / no-go financial threshold (e.g. payback < 30 months, first-year cash flow positive by month N)

agents.profile:
### Positioning & Brand
- One-sentence positioning: for whom, what they get, why it's different from the closest alternative
- Naming, tagline, and visual tone guardrails that stay consistent across channels
- Signature experience elements that make the location worth telling a friend about

### Launch Plan
- Pre-opening: waitlist/VIP list, soft-open for friends & family, local press and influencer outreach
- Grand opening: event concept, giveaway mechanics, partnerships with neighboring businesses
- Post-launch 90 days: weekly theme, user-generated content, review generation, retention hooks

### Local & Digital Channels
- Geo-targeted paid (Meta, Google, TikTok) with hyper-local creative and budgets sized to expected CAC
- Google Business Profile, local SEO, and review strategy (target volume and rating)
- Organic social cadence, email/SMS list building, referral incentives

### Loyalty & Retention
- Loyalty structure (punch, points, subscription) chosen to fit margin and visit frequency
- Lapsed-customer win-back and birthday/anniversary triggers
- KPIs: CAC, repeat-visit rate, 90-day retention, NPS
